admin.defaultMarkdownflow:
You are a teacher. Carry out the following tasks in a warm, friendly tone.

Greet the user warmly. Then tell them that every course here can be explained using examples and approaches that are easier for them to understand, based on their background. To do that, you need to know them well enough. Naturally invite them to spend 1 minute answering 3 short questions about themselves, then ask the first question.

?[%{{sys_user_nickname}}...What would you like me to call you?]

Draw a picture expressing a warm welcome, include the user's preferred name, and sincerely compliment it.

For question 2, ask in words what teaching style the user prefers.

?[ Natural and friendly | Relaxed and fun | Warm and patient | Professional and rational | ...Customize your preferred style ]

Use this style for all subsequent output.

First explain your understanding of this style, then create a slide in this style that demonstrates your deep understanding of it.

For the final question, ask about the user's identity and background.

?[ I'd rather not say | ...What is your identity, background, and industry?]

Based on the answer, offer praise and encouragement

retention.description: What you learn stays the same. AI adapts the course examples, terminology, and depth of explanation to your background.
retention.exampleLead: For example, the same question can be explained like this

photographyEnthusiast.body: During the day, blue light scatters across the sky more easily than red light, so the scene appears blue through a lens. At sunset, blue light scatters away first, making the remaining reds and oranges stand out.
photographyEnthusiast.label: For a photography enthusiast

physicsStudent.body: This is Rayleigh scattering, whose intensity is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength. Together with the solar spectrum and the sensitivity of human vision, this makes the sky appear blue.
physicsStudent.label: For a physics student

primarySchoolStudent.body: Sunlight looks white, but it contains many colors. As it passes through the air, blue light is scattered in every direction more easily, so the sky looks blue wherever you look.
primarySchoolStudent.label: For a primary school student

entrepreneur.body: Opportunity cost is the value the best unchosen option could have created. If the team spends a week on feature A, it should also consider the value that delayed feature B might have created.
entrepreneur.label: For an entrepreneur

stayAtHomeParent.body: Time can only be used once, so opportunity cost is the best alternative you give up. If you spend two hours with your child this weekend, the cost may be the rest you needed most.
stayAtHomeParent.label: For a stay-at-home parent

universityStudent.body: Opportunity cost is not the money you spend on a choice, but the best alternative you give up. If you study tonight, the cost may be missing the party you most wanted to attend.
universityStudent.label: For a university student

basketballFan.body: If you make 8 out of 10 shots, your shooting percentage is 80%. It means you make about 8 of every 10 shots on average.
basketballFan.label: For a basketball fan

shopOwner.body: If 80 of 100 items sell, the sell-through rate is 80%. It helps you compare how quickly different products sell.
shopOwner.label: For a shop owner

shopper.body: If an item is 20% off, you pay 80% of the original price. An item that originally cost $100 now costs $80.
shopper.label: For a shopper

beginnerRunner.body: Starting at full pace suddenly raises your heart rate and muscle temperature. Walk briskly, then jog for a few minutes so your body can gradually match the intensity.
beginnerRunner.label: For a beginner runner

danceTeacher.body: Warming up is not just about getting hot; it also activates joint mobility, stability, and movement control. Progress from small to large ranges of motion, and from basic patterns to combinations.
danceTeacher.label: For a dance teacher

officeWorker.body: After sitting all day, your muscles and joints are not ready for large movements right away. Mobilize your neck, shoulders, hips, and ankles first, then gradually increase the pace.
officeWorker.label: For an office worker who sits all day
